claims.text: Post-solidification annealing at 0.6–0.7 Tm will refine the lamellar interfaces in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Refining the lamellar interfaces through the proposed annealing treatment will increase room-temperature tensile strength.
Refining the lamellar interfaces through the proposed annealing treatment will increase room-temperature tensile ductility.
Conventionally cast eutectic high-entropy alloys can exhibit a dual-phase lamellar-colony microstructure.
Internal boundaries in the lamellar colonies serve as microcrack-initiation sites during room-temperature tensile loading.
An inert atmosphere during annealing will prevent oxidation.
Optimizing annealing time and cooling rate can refine the lamellar structure without causing coarsening.
Optimizing annealing time and cooling rate can avoid unwanted phase transformations.
The treatment will produce more uniform lamellar interfaces with fewer internal-boundary imperfections.
Reducing internal-boundary imperfections will lower local stress concentrations.
Lower local stress concentrations will reduce microcrack initiation.
Annealing near 0.65 Tm facilitates controlled atomic diffusion in the lamellar colonies.
Annealing-induced atomic diffusion repairs and sharpens internal lamellar boundaries.
Reducing boundary defect sites creates a better balance between dislocation motion and stress distribution.
The annealed alloy will show a statistically significant tensile-strength increase relative to the conventionally cast baseline.
The annealed alloy will show a statistically significant tensile-ductility increase relative to the conventionally cast baseline.
The annealed alloy will have a lower density of microcrack-initiation sites than the conventionally cast baseline.
The beneficial effects are restricted to an annealing-temperature window of approximately 0.6–0.7 Tm.
Substantial deviations in annealing temperature or duration may eliminate the beneficial effects.
Alloys with substantially different compositions or initial microstructures may not respond similarly to the treatment.
